azureDevOpsPullRequests.queries.markdown:
Specifies the categories shown in the Azure DevOps Pull Requests tree. Queries run against **the currently opened Azure DevOps repositories**. Each query object has a `label` shown in the tree and a `query` made of the supported qualifiers below. Use `default` for the built-in "Local Pull Request Branches" and "All Open" categories. Unsupported qualifiers and free-text search show an error on the category instead of being ignored.

**Supported qualifiers:**
 - `is:open`, `is:closed` (abandoned), `is:merged` (completed). Without a state qualifier, all states are listed.
 - `author:${user}` or `author:<identity ID>`
 - `review-requested:${user}` or `review-requested:<identity ID>`
 - `base:<target branch>`, `head:<source branch>`
 - `repo:${owner}/${repository}` (the current project and repository only)

**Variables available:**
 - `${user}` - the signed-in Azure DevOps identity
 - `${owner}` - the Azure DevOps project
 - `${repository}` - the repository name

**Example custom queries:**
```json
"azureDevOpsPullRequests.queries": [
  {
    "label": "Waiting For My Review",
    "query": "is:open review-requested:${user}"
  },
  {
    "label": "Targeting main",
    "query": "is:open base:main"
  }
]
```

azureDevOpsWorkItems.issueBranchTitle.ma.message:
Advanced settings for the name of the branch that is created when you start working on an issue. 
- `${user}` will be replaced with the currently logged in username 
- `${issueNumber}` will be replaced with the current issue number 
- `${issueType}` will be replaced with the issue type name (e.g. `Feature`, `Hotfix`). For branch-safe variants, use `${sanitizedIssueType}` or `${sanitizedLowercaseIssueType}` 
- `${sanitizedIssueTitle}` will be replaced with the issue title, with all spaces and unsupported characters (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-check-ref-format) removed. For lowercase, use `${sanitizedLowercaseIssueTitle}`

azureDevOpsWorkItems.queries.markdownDes: Specifies what queries should be used in the GitHub issues tree using [GitHub search syntax](https://help.github.com/en/articles/understanding-the-search-syntax) with variables.
